content.intro: {state} charges {stateRate} state sales tax on a vehicle, and most cities and counties add their own tax on top. Title and registration fees are small by comparison.

howItWorks.text: The state rate is {stateRate}. A trade-in comes off the price before tax, so only the net difference is taxed.
Cities and counties add their own tax. Only one city or county tax applies, and the dealer collects it for the place where the dealership is located.
A manufacturer rebate that you apply to the purchase price is still taxable. A rebate you take as cash is not.
If you bought in another state and bring the vehicle to Alabama, you get credit for tax you legally owed to that state.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the sales tax in Alabama?
faq.text: Yes. Tax is figured on the difference between the price and the trade-in credit. If the trade-in is worth more than the price, the extra cannot be deducted elsewhere.
Manufacturer and dealer rebates are taxable when applied to the purchase price. Federal electric vehicle credits are also subject to sales and use tax.

faq.q: Why do I have to enter my own local tax rate?
faq.text: Local rates vary by city and county and are not listed in the state's vehicle tax guide, so the calculator asks for the rate your dealer charges.
